text: I had headphones that I got from my brother for my birthday. And these headphones are noise-cancelling and they cost $300. I was walking in the hospital with these headphones on. It was very noisy in the hallway and I really liked that silence. My dad is in the room 412. And he was awake. And he looked at me and he doesn't recognize me very well. And he said, what is this? And I said, noise-cancelling headphones. And he said, what? I said, noise-cancelling headphones. He said, for noise? Yeah. How? I explained to him, I showed him the headphones. There are microphones. It listens to the room, to the noise in the room. And then it samples it thousands of times per second and it takes that sound wave and turns it upside down. It creates a mirror image of the wave. And then it plays that mirror image. So when the two waves meet, they cancel each other out. He said, so it meets itself and disappears? Yeah. And he said, you create silence with noise. And I said, it's either very smart or very sad. And he was very quiet and I said, both, and I laughed. And he said, when your mom died, I would wake up at night and listen to the house and the refrigerator, the clock, the wind outside. And I would listen to everything to not feel the silence. And he said, it's like being underwater, but not drowning. And he said, I mean, anti-noise. And he said, but if I speak, do I also cancel? I said, only if the microphone hears. He said, then don't let the microphone hear me. And then he grabbed my arm and he said, I want to tell you something. And then he said, I always thought silence was the opposite of sound. And it's not. Silence is when you stop fighting. And I didn't say anything. And I said, Dad, I'm here. And he said, mmm. And he closed his eyes. And I was just holding the headphones on his ears, even though my arm hurt. I was just listening. And I was imagining the waves meeting and cancelling.
